name: KTransformers
notable_features: Keeps attention and most of the dense weights on the GPU while streaming MoE experts from CPU RAM, so huge MoE models run on consumer GPUs
CPU-GPU expert scheduling, native BF16 and FP8 per-channel precision paths, and native RAWINT4 routed experts for Kimi K2.5/K2.6
Day-0 model support cadence (GLM-5, MiniMax-M2/M2.5/M3, Kimi-K2.5, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3-flash)
Also an SFT path: MoE LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning including block-FP8 LoRA and BF16 full fine-tuning, wired through LlamaFactory
AVX512 x86 including AMD servers, and an AVX2-only CPU backend for lower-end hosts
Ascend NPU support with CPU expert offload (DeepSeek-V4-Flash on a single NPU)
1M-token context and multimodal input on consumer GPUs via the GLM-5.3-flash path
Three-tier GPU-CPU-Disk prefix cache reuse, the only engine in this repo whose prefix cache has a disk tier - a consequence of its weights not fitting in VRAM rather than a design flourish
hardware_caveats: It is a research project first: the CPU-GPU split is tuned per model, and an unsupported architecture falls back to something much slower
The whole premise is that experts live in system RAM - you need enough RAM and memory bandwidth for the offloaded experts, and a discrete GPU is strongly implied for the resident half

CPU capability still gates throughput: AMX was originally required for the fine-tuning path, relaxed in v0.7.0 to compatible AVX512 x86, and an AVX2-only backend exists for inference but is a separate tutorial
Ascend NPU support is CPU-expert-offload dependent, so the NPU is not doing the expert math
Fine-tuning and inference are now split between kt-kernel and a LlamaFactory cookbook, and the original integrated framework was moved to archive/ - so docs and code are in two places
Day-0 support means a working tutorial, not parity with a datacenter engine on the same model
best_for: Running a very large MoE model on a consumer GPU with large system RAM, when datacenter hardware is not available
Researching heterogeneous placement and expert scheduling - that is what the project is for
MoE fine-tuning on a single workstation-class machine
avoid_for: Datacenter serving, where a CUDA-first engine with expert parallelism is the right tool
Dense models that fit comfortably in VRAM, where plain vLLM or llama.cpp is simpler
Production use without reading the per-model tutorial, because behaviour varies sharply per architecture
notes: Scheduling terms are approximate here: KTransformers is not a paged-KV serving engine in the vLLM sense. It does its own cache management plus CPU-GPU expert scheduling, so only 'prefix-cache' and 'expert-offload-scheduling' are recorded as literal mechanisms.
